Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin (OrcaSlicer fork, C++17, wxWidgets) has an in-app Agent (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/`) that sends the whole chat to a model provider on every call: Anthropic Messages (`AnthropicCodec.cpp`) or OpenAI Responses (`ResponsesCodec.cpp`), directly or through the JusPrin Cloud gateway, which forwards either format (`ProviderProfile.hpp`, `account_sign_in`). Today `AgentHost::make_agent_request` (around line 2800 of `AgentHost.cpp`) rebuilds the earlier turns on every request from the chat's messages and tool activities: assistant replies retold as text without thinking, tool calls replayed from `ToolActivity` records, app notes prefixed into user text ("JusPrin app note, not the person's words"), workspace blocks and plate pictures stripped from earlier messages, fired skills dropped from later requests. Every one of those makes the bytes differ from the request before, so provider prompt caches miss; about 70% of an Opus bill was cache writes. Kenneth (the owner) has decided the fix: each chat keeps an append-only record of every item ever sent to the model, a request renders that record plus the new items, nothing is rewritten or re-derived, and what the model should still see is a lifetime flag per item, never an edit. The full design, with roles, lifetimes, the provider-doc citations, risks and every decision (D1 to D9), is in the untracked `chat-history-cache-plan.md` in the main checkout `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin`; read it first, read `chat-history-cache-handoff.md` (sections 3 and 4) and `chat-history-measurement.md` next to it, and `.claude/worktrees/cache-invariant-test-51dab5/cache-rules.md` for provider cache rules. Never commit any of them. Your worktree is cut from the integration branch `claude/chat-history-cache` at `0807d77282`. It carries a hidden Catch2 guard, tag `[history-prefix]` in `tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp` (`agent_bridge_tests "[history-prefix]"`), that checks each turn's first request opens with the previous request's bytes on both wire formats; it fails today at 10 assertions and names the remaining leaks: workspace blocks on earlier messages, plate pictures, app notes, thinking, dropped skills. Already done on the branch: reminder deleted, trim and cut deleted, `object_import` always offered, `prompt_cache_key` on OpenAI, harness request logging. Chat records live in the managed project folder (`ProjectPersistence.cpp`, `ProjectStateDocument.cpp`, `state.json` written whole by write-then-rename after a debounce; attachment blobs under `attachments/<id>/<name>`), never in the 3MF. Rules: follow the error-handling discipline in `AGENTS.md` (no catch-and-continue, invariant violations propagate); every change must leave the code simpler or justify its growth in the commit message, and the production diff stat is recorded at merge; no live model calls at all (Kenneth approves paid batches individually; your evals run later against a baseline another session is recording now). Commit on your branch only, no push, no merge, never stage submodules, no attribution lines, temp notes untracked in the worktree root. Shared Mac build rules: check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja` first, pass `-- -j4`, one build per build directory, never restart a running build to change targets, run long builds with nohup in their own process group and watch the log, never end your turn to "wait for the build": block in the tool call. Build recipe for a fresh worktree (then build only `agent_bridge_tests`, always with the build dir as an absolute path): `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake -B <abs>/build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON -DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib`. A sibling session works in `tests/shell` and `tests/project_prompt` at the same time; stay in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/` and `tests/agent/`.

Task:
Replace the Agent's re-derived history with an append-only per-chat record that is rendered byte for byte on every request, so that the `[history-prefix]` guard passes on both wire formats and can be un-hidden. This is step R7 of the plan, and it carries R2 (skills) and R6 (notes) with it because the three are one model; R4 (workspace blocks) and R5 (pictures) fall out of "keep as sent". Read the plan doc's "Roles and lifetimes", "Gateway findings" and "R2 design point" sections before designing.

What the record is:
- Per chat, bound to one wire format (a chat talks to one provider family; D5: a model switch within the same format is allowed and only costs one cold cache; a switch across formats on an existing chat must be refused in `AgentHost::handle_set_chat_model` with a clear error, not silently re-rendered).
- Every item ever sent to the model, in order, with its exact wire content: the person's messages with what travelled with them (workspace block, plate picture, file report), assistant output including thinking or reasoning exactly as received (Anthropic thinking blocks with signatures; OpenAI reasoning items; check what each codec receives today and what the provider requires to be replayed), tool calls and results, fired skills, app notes.
- A lifetime per item, never an edit. Skills are visible only on the request that fired them (settled: on Anthropic via in-array `role:"system"` with `clear_at: "next_user_message"` and the beta header `mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`; on OpenAI as a `developer` item that has no clear and simply stays, so keep it as it is). App notes become operator-role in-conversation messages (Anthropic in-array `system`, OpenAI `developer`), kept visible, same for project and printer chats; this replaces the "JusPrin app note, not the person's words" user-text prefix. Tool results stay in their own channel.
- Pictures are stored as attachment-blob references and rendered inline at request time; image bytes never go into `state.json`.
- Stored in the chat document (`ProjectStateDocument`/`ProjectPersistence`), so a reopened project continues its chat with the same bytes. Design the migration for chats recorded before this change honestly: a one-time rendering of the old messages (plain person/assistant text, no tool replay) appended as the chat's first record items, after which nothing is re-derived; do not keep the legacy history builder alive beyond that one path, and say in the commit message what an old chat's model now sees.

Gateway constraint: the JusPrin Cloud gateway forwards messages and `cache_control` untouched but sends only its own configured headers, so the `clear_at` beta header does not reach Anthropic through it yet. Send `clear_at` and the header only when the profile is not `account_sign_in`; for the gateway path skills stay visible as on OpenAI. Make this a per-profile decision, never per-request, so one chat's rendering never changes. Note it in the report as the follow-up the gateway needs (add the header to the alias backend in `JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES`).

What to delete: the history re-derivation in `make_agent_request` (the `calls_by_message` replay of `ToolActivity` records into history entries, the text retelling of assistant replies, the note prefix, the stripping of workspace blocks and pictures, the skill-dropping) and anything that only served it. The expected outcome is less production code than before; if a part grows, say why in its commit message.

Tests: fake transports only (see `RecordingProvider`, `anthropic_stream`, `responses_stream` in `test_agent_bridge.cpp`). Add tests that encode the valid transitions: an item once sent is never changed; a later request is the earlier request plus appended items (for Anthropic, modulo the moving `cache_control` breakpoint on the newest user message; keep breakpoint placement as it is, never on a turn-scoped message); a cross-format switch is refused; an old chat migrates once; a reopened project renders the same bytes. Finally drop the `[.]` from the two guard cases so CTest runs them, and show the guard passing on both wire formats. Run the whole agent suite.

Commits: at least one for the record model and rendering (R7, including R4/R5), one for skill lifetime (R2), one for notes as operator role (R6), one for the cross-format refusal (D5), one un-hiding the guard. Each message says what changed, why, and the production diff direction. Done means: all commits on your branch, agent suite and guard green, and an untracked `r7-report.md` in the worktree root with the design as built, the migration behaviour, the production diff stat, the gateway follow-up, what the model now sees differently (this is a behaviour change and will be evaluated live later; list every difference), and anything unverified.

10	provider's prompt cache covers the whole conversation, not just the system prompt and tools.
11	Both Anthropic and OpenAI stay supported. Every past optimization that makes the history change

2	
3	Written 2026-10-28 for an agent who will take a whole-system view of the chat history the in-app Agent sends to the model. This is a working doc. Keep it untracked: don't commit it, and don't add it to `.gitignore`.

5	## 1. The problem in one paragraph
6	
7	Each time the in-app Agent calls the model, it resends the system prompt, the tool list and the whole chat so far. Providers bill the part they have seen before (the cached prefix) at a small fraction of the full price. During a turn, JusPrin resends exactly what it sent before, so the cache works. At the start of every new turn, though, the app's host rebuilds the earlier chat from its stored records in a different, shorter form. The provider has never seen that version, so it reads back only the system prompt and tool list (15,210 tokens on Opus 5.5) and writes everything after them into its cache again. Kenneth asked whether the history should simply never change. Before anyone rewrites how history is built, he wants each choice that makes it change understood. This document collects those choices, who made each one, and why.

46	## 4. Every way the history sent to the model changes between turns, and why

50	### 4.1 Earlier turns are retold as text: no thinking, no full response
51	- **What.** Each earlier turn is rebuilt from stored message text, plus each tool call with its stored result.
52	- **Origin.** `c5c27082ee`, 2026-09-01, made by Codex while building the first live OpenAI agent (Codex session `~/.codex/sessions/2026/09/01/rollout-2026-09-01T00-08-12-01a05bcc-….jsonl.zst`). Agent. No rationale is recorded. The only comment says "The provider gets bounded semantic history."

54	  - The Phase 5.1 handoff in that same commit forbids storing "provider response bodies" in the project 3MF, recovery files or logs, and a turn's thinking is part of those bodies.
55	  - `store:false` is used everywhere.

75	### 4.3 History is trimmed to 64 KiB

142	## 6. Options for a whole-system design (for discussion, nothing decided)
143	
144	- **A. Keep the prototype.** It works and is tested. It is complex because it checks two copies of the history against each other. It still misses the turn after a file load.
145	- **B. The host stores each turn as it was sent and only appends.**
146	  - The chat document keeps the provider-neutral record of every request's content: the person's words with their workspace block, skill text, the model's text and calls, and results as sent.
147	  - The loop then just appends, and its check shrinks to "same chat, and the last turn finished".
148	  - Questions to settle:
149	    - **Thinking.** Is it kept in memory only (lost on restart or provider switch, which costs one cache miss) or stored? Storing it conflicts with the 2026-09-01 rule against provider bodies in the 3MF (4.1).
150	    - **Pictures.** Kept as references to blobs, or dropped and replaced by a stable placeholder text (4.5).
151	    - **Old workspace blocks.** These keep stale state in the history (4.4). Kenneth's view on that is unknown.
152	    - **Trimming.** It becomes a rare, deliberate compaction (for example a summary) that knowingly starts a new cache, instead of a rolling cut (4.3).
153	    - **The file-load reminder.** Moves into the file-load message itself, or is always present (4.6).
154	    - **Notes.** Either appended where they happened, which reverses Kenneth's 2026-09-07 call, or never sent. The current half-way state is the worst for consistency (4.7).

156	  - Stop the reminder flipping, and trim only rarely.
157	  - Add a cache marker at the end of the retold history (Anthropic only reads cache at marked positions, and looks back at most 20 blocks from each marker).
158	  - This saves only the older turns. The turn that just ended is still rewritten at every turn start, which is where most of the money goes.

1	# Provider prompt-caching rules, and where JusPrin's codecs fall short
2	
3	Working doc, 2026-10-28, for the chat-history cache plan (task M2). Untracked: never commit it, never add it to `.gitignore`.
4	
5	Both providers cache only an unchanged opening of the request, so an append-only history is necessary on both. It is not enough on either. Anthropic also needs cache markers in the right places, the same thinking and effort settings, and a request within 5 minutes (or 1 hour at extra cost). OpenAI needs requests routed to the same machine, which for the model JusPrin uses means a `prompt_cache_key`; JusPrin sends none. Every rule below was read from the provider's docs on 2026-10-28. "Inference" marks what I concluded rather than read.
6	
7	Sources:
8	- [A1] Anthropic prompt caching: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching
9	- [A2] Anthropic thinking: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking
10	- [A3] Anthropic preserved thinking: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/preserved-thinking
11	- [O1] OpenAI prompt caching: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching
12	- [O2] OpenAI reasoning: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/reasoning
13	
14	## 1. Anthropic (Messages API, `AnthropicCodec.cpp`)
15	
16	| Topic | Rule | Source |
17	|---|---|---|
18	| Identical prefix | "Cache hits require 100 percent identical prompt segments, including all text and images up to and including the block marked with cache control." | A1 |
19	| Prefix order | The prefix is `tools`, then `system`, then `messages`, in that order. A change at one level invalidates that level and every later one. | A1 |
20	| Markers | Caching happens only at `cache_control` breakpoints, or at the automatic one a top-level `cache_control` adds. "Marking a block with `cache_control` writes exactly one cache entry"; no entry is written for any earlier position. At most 4 breakpoints per request, and the automatic one takes one of the 4. | A1 |
21	| Where markers may go | Tool definitions, `system` blocks, text blocks in user and assistant turns, images and documents in user turns, `tool_use` and `tool_result` blocks. Not on thinking blocks, citations or empty text blocks. | A1 |
22	| Moving a marker | Moving a breakpoint is the documented pattern for a growing chat ("the fourth breakpoint moved to that new final message"). `cache_control` markers sit outside the thinking prefix check: adding, moving or removing them is not an edit. | A1, A3 |
23	| Lookback | A read looks for an earlier write at the breakpoint, then walks back one block at a time, "at most 20 positions for each breakpoint". A run of consecutive `tool_use` blocks counts as one position, and so does a run of `tool_result` blocks. | A1 |
24	| Timing | An entry can be read only after the response that wrote it has started. | A1 |
25	| Minimum length | 512 tokens for Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, Fable 5/5.1 and Mythos 5/5.1. 1,024 tokens for Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5 and Sonnet 4.x. 2,048 for Opus 4.7. 4,096 for Opus 4.5 and 4.6. A shorter prompt is processed uncached, with no error. | A1 |
26	| TTL | 5 minutes by default, refreshed free on every read. A 1-hour TTL is available with `"ttl": "1h"`. A longer TTL must come before a shorter one in the request. The lifetime runs from the start of the request. | A1 |
27	| Price (multiples of the input price) | Writes: 1.25x for 5 minutes, 2x for 1 hour. Reads: 0.1x by default, 0.05x on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5. | A1 |
28	| What else invalidates | Tool definitions invalidate everything. `tool_choice` invalidates messages. Adding or removing an image anywhere invalidates messages. A thinking or `output_config.effort` change always invalidates messages, and on some models tools and system too. Per-message effort (a `role: "system"` message, beta) leaves the prefix intact. | A1, A2 |
29	| Thinking in history | Opus 4.5+, Sonnet 4.6+, Haiku 5.5, Fable and Mythos keep every earlier turn's thinking in context, and the cache stays valid when a new user message is added. Earlier models strip earlier turns' thinking, so messages after it leave the cache. A thinking block the current model cannot read (another model's) is dropped, and the cached prefix changes from that block on. | A1, A2 |
30	| Edits and thinking (correctness, not just cost) | A thinking block is valid only while `system`, `tools` and every message before it are unchanged. For accounts created on or after 2026-08-31 the API checks this on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 and Fable 5.1, and by default rejects an edited prefix with a 400. With `drop_block` it drops the block and "the prompt cache restarts at the edit". The listed edits include: adding a text block to an earlier user turn or removing one you added last time; re-rendering context in the first user message with a changed value; shortening an earlier `tool_result` or re-encoding an earlier image; changing `system` or `tools`; removing thinking from the middle of the history. Appending at the end and changing `effort`, `max_tokens`, `tool_choice` or `cache_control` are not edits. | A3 |
31	| Mid-conversation system messages | A `role: "system"` message inside `messages` is supported on current models (not Sonnet 5). In a tool loop it goes after the `tool_result` message, never between `tool_use` and `tool_result`. "Once sent, the message is part of the prefix for later thinking: leave it in place on later requests." | A1, A3 |
32	| Usage | `cache_read_input_tokens` are tokens read; `cache_creation_input_tokens` are tokens written, broken down by TTL in `cache_creation.ephemeral_5m_input_tokens` / `ephemeral_1h_input_tokens`. `input_tokens` are only the tokens after the last breakpoint. Total input = read + creation + input_tokens. | A1 |
33	
34	## 2. OpenAI (Responses API, `ResponsesCodec.cpp`)
35	
36	JusPrin's OpenAI default is `gpt-5.4-mini`, a model from before GPT-5.6, so the "earlier models" rules apply. OpenRouter's caching is not covered here.
37	
38	| Topic | Rule | Source |
39	|---|---|---|
40	| Identical prefix | "Cache reuse requires the entire rendered prefix to match." OpenAI caches the full rendered context: instructions, developer messages, tool definitions, and history with text, images and documents. | O1 |
41	| Markers | Before GPT-5.6: none. Caching is on by default and "Only implicit caching is supported", with breakpoints placed by OpenAI at model-dependent intervals. GPT-5.6+: `prompt_cache_options.mode` is `implicit` or `explicit`. Explicit mode takes `prompt_cache_breakpoint` on content blocks inside input messages, never on top-level `instructions`. With no breakpoint placed, explicit mode does not cache at all. Up to 4 writes per request. Implicit mode puts a breakpoint at the end of the latest eligible message and looks back over "up to 20 earlier eligible message endings". The docs do not say which mode is the default. | O1 |
42	| Routing | Requests go to a machine chosen by "a hash of the initial tokens after the hidden OpenAI content, including tool definitions". The cache lives on that machine. "traffic above 15 requests per minute can lead to overflow routing", and an overflowed request misses. Before GPT-5.6, `prompt_cache_key` "separates cache reuse between groups of requests and helps optimize cache routing"; the advice is about 15 requests per minute per key. GPT-5.6+ does not need the key. | O1 |
43	| Minimum length | 1,024 visible input tokens on GPT-5.6+. For earlier models it "varies by request settings" (tools, images, schemas, effort, verbosity). Earlier models report `cached_tokens` rounded down to a multiple of 128. | O1 |
44	| Retention | Earlier models, in memory: "around 5 to 10 minutes of inactivity, up to one hour". Extended `24h` retention (`prompt_cache_retention`) is listed for `gpt-5.5`, `gpt-5.4`, `gpt-5.2`, `gpt-5.1`, `gpt-5` and others. `gpt-5.4-mini` is not on that list. Organizations without Zero Data Retention default to `24h`. GPT-5.6+: `prompt_cache_options.ttl` of `30m` (default) or `12h`. | O1 |
45	| Price | Earlier models: no write charge, reads at 0.1x. GPT-5.6+: writes at 1.25x (30 minutes) or 2.5x (12 hours). | O1 |
46	| What else changes the prefix | `model`, `tools` (names, descriptions, schemas, order), `parallel_tool_calls`, `text.format`, `reasoning.effort`, `text.verbosity`, `context_management`. A `configuration_update` input item changes effort without breaking the prefix (GPT-6). | O1, O2 |
47	| Reasoning in history | Within a tool loop, pass back every reasoning item with its call. Models before GPT-5.6 do not render earlier turns' reasoning into the next sample; GPT-5.6 renders it by default. With `store: false`, reasoning items carry `encrypted_content` by default; `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]` is still accepted but no longer required. Neither guide says how reasoning items affect cache hits. | O2 |
48	| Usage | `usage.input_tokens_details.cached_tokens` is billed reads, excluding writes. On GPT-5.6+, `cache_write_tokens` gives writes, split into `ttl_30m_tokens` and `ttl_12h_tokens`. | O1 |
49	
50	Inference, not stated in the docs: on a pre-5.6 model, the last request of turn N renders that turn's reasoning, and the first request of turn N+1 no longer does (it is now an earlier turn's reasoning). If that is how rendering works, the rendered prefix changes at turn N's first reasoning item even when JusPrin resends the input byte for byte. In that case, on `gpt-5.4-mini` an append-only history can win back only the turns before the last one. This needs a live check of `cached_tokens` (one cheap OpenAI run, needs Kenneth's approval).
51	
52	## 3. What the codecs do today
53	
54	`AnthropicCodec.cpp` places three breakpoints, all with the default 5-minute TTL:
55	1. on the last tool (`tools_json`, line 87);
56	2. on the single `system` block (`build`, line 272);
57	3. on the last block of the newest `user` message (`build`, line 262). It moves forward on every request.
58	
59	It sends `thinking: adaptive` and `output_config.effort` from the chat's model choice, replays each response's own blocks (thinking included) within a turn, keeps fired skills in place for the rest of the turn, and reads `cache_read_input_tokens` and `cache_creation_input_tokens`.
60	
61	`ResponsesCodec.cpp` sends `store: false`, `parallel_tool_calls: true`, `instructions`, `tools`, `input`, and `reasoning.effort` when set. It sends no `prompt_cache_key`, no `prompt_cache_retention` and no `include`. It replays each response's own items (reasoning included) within a turn. It sends fired skills only as the last items of the request where they fired, and drops them from the next request. It reads `cached_tokens` only.
62	
63	## 4. Gaps
64	
65	The first three are what the guard test in `tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp` (`[history-prefix]`) catches; the rest it cannot see, because they are about markers, settings, timing or routing, not the bytes of the history.
66	
67	1. **Earlier turns are rewritten between turns (both codecs).** The host replays them as text: no thinking, no workspace block, no pictures, no skills, results as stored, app notes missing. This breaks the identical-prefix rule [A1, O1]. On Anthropic, once thinking is carried across turns (plan step R7), the same edits become 400 errors for accounts created after 2026-08-31 [A3]. Removing a workspace block from an earlier user turn, re-rendering the file-load reminder in the first message, and cutting a stored result are each named as edits there.
68	2. **Responses drops a fired skill from the next request** (mid-turn, and on the next turn). That changes the middle of the input [O1]. Anthropic's codec already keeps them, which matches "leave it in place on later requests" [A3].
69	3. **The file-load reminder at the start of the history appears and disappears** (handoff 4.6). That is a changed first message, the worst place for an edit [A1, A3, O1].
70	4. **No `prompt_cache_key` on Responses.** Every JusPrin user sends the same instructions and tools, so before GPT-5.6 all of them hash to the same machines. Above about 15 requests per minute across all users, requests overflow to other machines and miss [O1]. A per-chat key (for example the project and chat id) keeps each chat on one machine. GPT-5.6+ does not need it.
71	5. **5-minute TTL on Anthropic, in-memory retention on `gpt-5.4-mini`.** A pause longer than 5 minutes (the vase journey had a 6-minute one) loses the whole Anthropic cache, and the next request writes it all again at 1.25x [A1]. Anthropic offers a 1-hour TTL at 2x per write. On OpenAI, `gpt-5.4-mini` is not listed for 24-hour retention, so its entries last 5 to 10 idle minutes [O1]. Whether 1 hour pays depends on how often people pause: it is a measurement question, not a fix.
72	6. **A mid-chat thinking or effort change restarts the cache on both providers** [A1, A2, O1]. The per-chat thinking picker (`1ca65bb087`) allows this. Anthropic's per-message effort (beta) and OpenAI's `configuration_update` (GPT-6) avoid it; neither is used. Model switches start a new cache on any design.
73	7. **Cache writes are not reported by TTL.** The Anthropic codec ignores `cache_creation.ephemeral_5m/1h_input_tokens`. That only matters once a 1-hour TTL is used. The Responses codec ignores `cache_write_tokens`, which only GPT-5.6+ reports and charges for.
74	8. **Lookback distance (low risk).** The moving Anthropic breakpoint is about 3 to 6 positions past the previous write in a normal turn: the response's thinking, text and calls, then the results. The window is 20 positions, and runs of `tool_use` or `tool_result` blocks count as one [A1]. A single response that interleaves more than about 18 thinking and call blocks would miss. Nothing seen so far comes close. A second moving breakpoint would cover it.
75	9. **OpenAI explicit mode (future).** If JusPrin moves to GPT-5.6+ and explicit mode turns out to be the default, a request without `prompt_cache_breakpoint` is not cached at all [O1]. The Responses codec places none. Check the default before switching models.
76	
77	Not a gap: the Anthropic tool and system breakpoints are at the end of fixed content, as recommended [A1]. Prompts are far above the minimum length (about 15,000 tokens of tools and system). The moving breakpoint follows the documented pattern. The Responses codec already gets `encrypted_content` with `store: false` by default [O2].

## 1. Placement rules

Content-carrying system messages:

> A mid-conversation system message that carries content (`text`, `tool_addition`, or `tool_removal` blocks) must immediately follow a `user` turn (or an `assistant` turn ending in a server tool result), and must either be the last entry in `messages` or be immediately followed by an `assistant` turn. A `user` message that carries `tool_result` blocks counts: in an agentic loop you can place the system message right after the tool results, before Claude's next turn. Any other position for a message that carries content, including between an `assistant` `tool_use` block and the `tool_result` that answers it, returns a 400 error. A message with empty `content` that only sets [`output_config.effort`] is accepted anywhere in `messages`. Consecutive `system` messages are judged together, so an effort-only message next to one that carries content follows the rule for content.

Turn-scoped messages:

> A turn-scoped system message must follow a `user` turn (or an `assistant` turn ending in a server tool result) and precede an `assistant` turn or end the array, like any mid-conversation system message. One that ends the array always renders. One followed directly by another `user` message is a 400 error, not a cleared message.

Implications:
- A content-carrying system message cannot be first, cannot follow an `assistant` turn (other than one ending in a server tool result), and cannot sit between a `tool_use` and its `tool_result`.
- The page doesn't explicitly say whether two adjacent system messages are allowed. It only says consecutive system messages are judged together.

## 2. Shape, `clear_at`, and beta header

A system message is `"role": "system"` with `content` and, optionally, `clear_at`:

```json
{
  "role": "system",
  "clear_at": "next_user_message",
  "content": "Request independent reads in one turn."
}
```

> To scope a `role: "system"` message to the current turn, set its `clear_at` field. It takes one of two values:
> * `"never"` (the default): the message renders at its position on every request that includes it. Omitting the field is identical.
> * `"next_user_message"`: the message is **turn-scoped**. Its text renders only while no `role: "user"` message comes after it in `messages`.

Beta header: `mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`.

> Turn-scoped system messages are in beta. Include the beta header `mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`. Without it, `clear_at` is rejected as an unknown field.

## 3. What clearing does and what must be re-sent

> Once a later user message exists, the message is **cleared**: it stays in the array but renders nothing and costs no input tokens, on that request and every later one.

> **Resend cleared messages verbatim.** A cleared message is still part of the conversation history. Rebuilding it from current state (a fresh token count, a timestamp), dropping it as redundant, or changing its `clear_at` value is an edit to an earlier message. So the message must stay in the array unchanged. Only its rendering stops.

For turn-scoped messages, it is not allowed:

> **No `cache_control` on its blocks.** A cleared message is never part of a cache key, so a breakpoint on it could never match. Put the breakpoint on the last block of the preceding user turn instead.

The page doesn't state whether `cache_control` is allowed on a non-turn-scoped system message. The error list includes only the turn-scoped restriction.

> This feature is available on Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Mythos 5.1, Claude Fable 5, Claude Mythos 5, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Opus 5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, and Claude Haiku 5.5. ... This feature is not available on Claude Sonnet 5. Use the top-level `system` field there instead.

Plain string or array of blocks:

> Use a plain string or content blocks for `content`, the same as a `user` or `assistant` turn.

Now each chat keeps a record in the project document of every item the
model was sent, and every request is that record followed by what the turn
has added so far:

- the person's messages, each with its print-issue context, workspace
  block, attachment listing, and picture or PDF parts as first sent; a
  file-load report as the turn's own words;
- the model's output exactly as the provider returned it, thinking or
  reasoning included (Responses items keep their ids);
- tool results in their own channel, pictures included;
- fired skills (their picture, then their text in the operator role) and
  the printer chat's notes as operator messages.

Items are only appended, never edited. ProviderAgent hands the host the
items a later request can follow on from: the person's side once a request
carrying it was accepted, each response with its results once the next
request went, the end of the turn when it completes. A trailing operator
message or a call without its result is never recorded. Picture and PDF
bytes go to blobs under attachments/chat-<id>/ beside the attachment
blobs; the document stores only their paths, and a reopened project reads
them back, so it renders the same bytes. Deleting a chat removes its blob
directory. A record is bound to the wire format it was written in; giving
it to the other format is a logic error (the model switch is refused
earlier in a following commit).

What an old chat's model now sees: a chat that talked before this change

longer sees the earlier calls it used to get replayed. Messages after that
last reply go as any unsent message does.
